newsitem.title: USA: TeleCheck says US Feb same-store sales up 2.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: TeleCheck says US Feb same-store sales up 2.3 pct.

text.p: Same-store retail spending in February rose a moderate 2.3 percent over the same period last year, data compiled by TeleCheck Services Inc showed Tuesday.
The growth rate was in line with the steady but modest pace of the country's economic growth, said William Ford, TeleCheck's senior economic adviser.

"Retail spending may be tempered by consumers' heavy debt burdens and by the baby boomers' greater attention to increasing their savings and moderating their spending as they prepare for retirement," he added.

TeleCheck said retail sales rose 5.4 percent in the Southwest, 4.3 percent in the Southeast, 2.9 percent in the Mid-Atlantic, 1.5 percent in the Midwest, 1.3 percent in the West and 0.2 percent in the Northeast.

The TeleCheck Retail Index is based on a year-over-year, same-store comparison of the dollar volume of checks written by consumers at more than 27,000 of TeleCheck's 160,000 subscribing locations. Figures are not adjusted for inflation.
TeleCheck is a subsidiary of First Data Corp.
